title: Closing a review captures no mandatory justification note — `RevisionModal` uses `resolvedNoteRequired = noteRequired ?? !isClose`; when `targetState === 'closed'` note is optional; approval decisions have no documented basis; violates ISO 19011:2018 §6.4.9
statusRaw: Already fixed in the live code — RevisionModal.jsx hardcodes resolvedNoteRequired = true, with a 30-char minimum enforced when closing (isClose branch). No code change was needed; verified by reading the current file, not by making an edit.
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/trust-vault/RevisionModal.jsx

Root Cause: `resolvedNoteRequired = noteRequired ?? !isClose` — when `targetState === 'closed'`, `isClose` is `true`, so `resolvedNoteRequired` evaluates to `false`. The note field is optional precisely when it should be mandatory.

Impact: Every certification approval creates a workflow record with a blank justification. ISO 19011:2018 §6.4.9 requires documented basis for review decisions. No approval in the system has a verifiable rationale.

Claude Fix Prompt: Change to `resolvedNoteRequired = noteRequired ?? true` — always require a note. Add minimum length: in the submit handler, `if (!resolvedNote || resolvedNote.trim().length < 30) { setError('Justification required (minimum 30 characters) when closing a review'); return; }`.

title: Revoking a certification captures no mandatory reason — `WorkflowActionPanel` `revoke` action key has no `modal: 'note'` prop; calls `transitionCertification` directly with no note parameter; revocation has no documented rationale; violates ISO 27001:2022 Annex A 5.33
statusRaw: FIXED — verified 2026-09-02 against the checked-out feature/dev (client-panel HEAD 0b8712ce). WorkflowActionPanel.jsx:67 has `modal: 'note'` on the revoke action; the handler at line 219 routes it to onNote; CertificationCard.jsx:76,352,450-459 has the previously-missing noteModal state, onNote wiring, and a second RevisionModal instance for the note dialog; RevisionModal.jsx gives revoke its own title/color/copy and requires a non-empty reason (isRevoke branch, meetsMinLength = noteLength > 0) sent as { note } to POST /certifications/:id/transition, which the backend persists.
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/trust-vault/WorkflowActionPanel.jsx

Root Cause: The `revoke` action key in `CERT_STATUS_ACTIONS` has no `modal: 'note'` prop. `transitionCertification` is called directly with only `targetState: 'revoked'` — no reason string is ever sent to the API.

Impact: Revocation records contain no documented rationale. ISO 27001:2022 Annex A 5.33 requires documented handling of certification changes. Auditors reviewing revocations will find blank reason fields throughout.

Claude Fix Prompt: In `CERT_STATUS_ACTIONS`, add to the `revoke` entry: `modal: 'note', noteRequired: true, noteMinLength: 50, notePlaceholder: 'Reason for revocation (required — minimum 50 characters)'`. Wire `transitionNote` through `onTransition(targetState, note)` → `POST /certifications/:id/revoke` with `{reason: note}`.
fixEvidence: `WorkflowActionPanel.jsx:67,219` (modal:'note' + onNote routing) + `CertificationCard.jsx:76,352,450-459` (noteModal state/wiring that was previously entirely absent) + `RevisionModal.jsx:62-64,80,98` (revoke-specific copy/color, mandatory non-empty reason, sent as {note} to the generic transition endpoint) — traced end-to-end and confirmed working on 2026-09-02. **Minor deviation from the fix prompt, not blocking:** revoke requires only a non-empty reason, not the suggested 50-character minimum (that threshold is applied only to the 'close'/Approve action, MIN_CLOSE_NOTE_LENGTH=30). The core defect — revocation previously sent zero reason at all — is closed; a stricter length floor for revoke specifically would be a reasonable follow-up, not a fix gap. No regression found — the shared RevisionModal correctly branches behavior by targetState across close/revoke/needs_revision without breaking the pre-existing flows.

title: Self-review not prevented — `MyReviewsTab` shows entities where `currentUser` is assigned reviewer with no guard against `currentUser._id === entity.createdBy._id`; submitter can approve own document; violates ISO 27001:2022 Annex A 5.3
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/trust-vault/MyReviewsTab.jsx

Root Cause: `MyReviewsTab` renders all entities where `currentUser` is assigned as reviewer with no guard checking whether `currentUser._id === entity.createdBy._id`. The document submitter can be assigned as its own reviewer.

Impact: The certification review process provides no segregation of duties. ISO 27001:2022 Annex A 5.3 is violated. Auditors sampling reviewed certifications may find the submitter and reviewer are the same person.

Claude Fix Prompt: In `MyReviewsTab`, filter items before rendering: `const reviewableItems = items.filter(e => String(e.createdBy?._id) !== String(currentUser._id));`. Display a notice: `{items.length !== reviewableItems.length && <Alert>Some items were hidden because you are the submitter — segregation of duties requires an independent reviewer.</Alert>}`. Add backend guard on review submit endpoint.
